events.title: John Glenn Orbits the Earth
events.description: Aboard the Mercury spacecraft Friendship 7, astronaut John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth, completing three orbits in about 4 hours and 55 minutes before splashing down in the Atlantic Ocean.
events.significance: Glenn's flight helped restore American confidence in the Space Race against the Soviet Union and was a key step toward the Apollo program and crewed lunar missions.

events.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art Opens in New York City
events.description: The Metropolitan Museum of Art opened to the public in its first location at 681 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, after being founded in 1870 by a group of American businessmen, artists, and philanthropists.
events.significance: The museum grew into one of the largest and most visited art museums in the world, with a collection spanning five thousand years of human creativity.

events.title: Battle of Kasserine Pass Concludes
events.description: The Battle of Kasserine Pass in Tunisia, which began on February 19, continued through February 20 as Axis forces under Erwin Rommel pushed back American and Allied troops in the first major engagement between U.S. and German forces in the North African campaign.
events.significance: Although a setback for the Americans, the battle exposed weaknesses in U.S. command and tactics, leading to significant reforms that improved performance in later campaigns.

events.title: Ranger 8 Crashes into the Moon
events.description: NASA's Ranger 8 spacecraft impacted the lunar surface in the Sea of Tranquility after transmitting over 7,000 high-resolution photographs of the Moon's surface.
events.significance: The images helped NASA scout and evaluate potential landing sites for the Apollo missions, contributing directly to the planning of the first crewed Moon landing.

events.title: Birth of Ground-Breaking Era in Spanish Politics Continues
events.description: On February 20, 1976, Spain was in the midst of its transition following Franco's declining rule, a period leading to democratic reform after his death in November 1975.
events.significance: This period set the stage for Spain's peaceful transition to democracy under King Juan Carlos I.
